remediated_findings.original_finding: tests/support/disabled-nav-item-pattern.ts:27 -- nav label interpolated into RegExp without escaping regex metacharacters
remediated_findings.reviewer_evidence: Confirmed escapeRegExp is byte-identical to the MDN idiom and to both files it claims to match. Empirically swept 22 metacharacters and 11 label shapes (well beyond the implementer's own 3 test cases), including a balanced-parens case ("a(b)c") the implementer had not tested, which pre-fix silently became a capture group (no throw, wrong match) and post-fix is correctly rejected. Confirmed byte-for-byte identical regex .source for both real disabled-item labels (Evidence, Internal review) before and after the escape -- proving zero behavioral change for anything the product actually renders today.

new_yellow_findings.summary: The identical buggy inline regex construction that S1 finding #1 (in shell.spec.ts) was raised about still exists verbatim in these two sibling specs, unaffected by the shell.spec.ts extraction. Proven empirically live against the two real disabled sidebar items (Evidence, Internal review) in producer-auth-smoke.spec.ts specifically -- the assertion there would not actually catch a regression to the sr-only reason text, contrary to its own adjacent comment's claim. Pre-existing (predates S1 entirely), test-only, latent (E2E did not run in the reviewer's environment or in CI historically per the file's own comment). Not introduced or claimed-fixed by 8d95738. Recommended as a tracked follow-up, not a blocker.

Test titled '...matches only that exact literal accessible name' asserts only the positive case, no negative -- would not fail if the pattern were over-permissive. Largely duplicative of the adjacent unbalanced-paren throw test. Correctness of the implementation is unaffected (reviewer independently verified the negative case holds); this is test-naming precision only.
